transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve realized I’m planning a lot of my day around avoiding elevators. Like, I’ll take five flights of stairs at my apartment instead, and I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I also stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another way up. It’s starting to get in the way.
Do you experience panic or intense fear when you think about being in an elevator?

Yes. I mean, I know elevators in office buildings are probably safe, but when I’m looking at the old doors in my apartment building or at work, my brain kind of treats it like I’m about to get stuck in there or it’s going to drop. Part of me knows that’s over the top, but the fear still kicks in.
Do you experience similar fears or anxieties in other small or enclosed spaces, like cars or tunnels?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed it much with cars or tunnels. It seems to be mainly elevators for me.
Is your fear limited to elevators or do you also fear the possibility of being trapped or stuck in them?

It’s mostly elevators, but yeah, the fear is really about getting trapped in one—or it suddenly dropping. I know, like, an office elevator is probably safe, but when I see the older doors at my apartment or at work, my mind just goes there anyway.
Have you ever felt this fear of being trapped in any situation other than an elevator?
Not that I can think of. I mean, I don’t really get that same trapped feeling in other places—it’s been pretty much just elevators.
Are you afraid of other small, enclosed spaces that have doors which close, like closets or small rooms?
No, I don’t think so. Closets or small rooms don’t really bother me in that way. It’s more just elevators.
Have you ever had a situation in an elevator where your fear came true, such as getting stuck?
No, I don’t think that’s ever actually happened. I haven’t been stuck in one or anything like that. It’s more the thought of it happening that gets to me.
Do you think your fear would decrease if you were in an elevator with someone you trust?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to whether it changes when I’m with someone I trust. I guess it might help a little, but I don’t know for sure.
Is your fear of elevators related to the fear of not being able to get out if something happens?

Yeah, I think that’s a big part of it. I know logically an elevator in an office building is probably safe, but when I see the older doors in my apartment building or at work, my mind goes straight to, like, what if I can’t get out, or what if it drops. I know that’s probably over the top, but that’s where my head goes.
Is your fear of elevators specifically about the elevator, or is it more about the feeling of being trapped that happens to occur in an elevator?

I think it’s more the feeling of being trapped, but the elevator is what sets it off. Like, I know an elevator in an office building is probably safe, but when I see the older doors in my apartment or at work, my mind treats it like I’m about to get stuck or dropped. Part of me knows that’s kind of over the top, but it still happens.
Do you think you would fear being trapped in other types of situations where escape might be difficult, even if they are not enclosed spaces like elevators?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it in other situations like that. It mostly comes up with elevators for me, so I don’t know if I’d react the same way somewhere else.
Would you say your fear is about elevators themselves or is it more about the possibility of being trapped, regardless of where it happens?

I’d say it’s more the possibility of being trapped, but elevators are really the thing that brings it up for me. Like, I know an office elevator is probably safe, but when I see those older doors in my apartment building or at work, my mind just goes to, “What if I get stuck or it drops?” Even though part of me knows that’s probably over the top.
Have you ever experienced a similar feeling of fear or anxiety in a situation where you felt a loss of control, even if it wasn't in an enclosed space like an elevator?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a clear example outside of elevators where I felt that same kind of fear. It mostly seems tied to that situation for me.
Do you think your fear of being trapped would be triggered by other modes of transportation, like a train or a bus, if you were unable to get off when you wanted to?

I’m not really sure. I take buses and trains sometimes, and I haven’t noticed the same reaction there. I guess if I really couldn’t get off, maybe it could bother me, but I don’t know that it’s the same as with elevators.
Would your fear decrease if you were in a situation where you felt trapped, but it wasn't an elevator?

Yeah, I think it probably would be less if it wasn’t an elevator. I mean, the trapped feeling is part of it, but elevators are what really set it off for me. Like with the old doors in my apartment building or at work, my mind jumps to getting stuck or it dropping, even though I know that sounds kind of over the top.
Would you say your fear is specifically about the elevator itself, or could it also be triggered by other situations where you feel trapped?

It feels more specific to the elevator itself. I know, logically, an elevator in an office building is probably safe, but when I see those older doors in my apartment or at work, my mind goes right to getting trapped or the elevator dropping. Part of me knows that’s probably over the top, but it still hits me that way.
Would you feel anxious or afraid if you were in a situation where you couldn't leave, but it had nothing to do with an elevator?

Probably not as much. If it had nothing to do with an elevator, I might be uncomfortable, but the real fear seems to happen when I’m looking at an elevator, especially those older doors at my apartment or work. Even though I know it’s probably safe, my mind goes right to getting stuck or it dropping.
Would you feel anxious or afraid if you were trapped in a situation that had nothing to do with elevators, such as being in a crowded room with no clear exit?

I might feel a little uneasy, but not really the same kind of afraid. For me it’s more the elevator itself. Like, I know an elevator in an office building is probably safe, but when I see those old elevator doors at my apartment or at work, my brain just goes to, “I’m going to get trapped,” or “it’s going to drop,” even though I know that sounds kind of over the top.
Would your fear of being trapped in an elevator decrease if you knew you could escape or be rescued quickly?

Maybe a little, yeah, if I really knew someone could get me out fast. But honestly, when I’m standing there looking at those old elevator doors at my apartment or work, my mind still jumps to getting trapped or the elevator dropping. I know an office elevator is probably safe, and part of me knows I’m overreacting, but it still feels that way in the moment.
